Well, I have a workaround at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-cpptools/pull/14457 , but it's not an ideal experience in the manually invoked case, because users need to manually cancel the Find All References when a 2nd is made, because the 1st results won't appear in the UI so it'll be a waste of time computing them.

And there are still bugs with our "other references" window being overwritten by the Copilot invoked Find All References and Cancel being used in our notification UI causing Copilot to think there are 0 references instead of the operation being cancelled -- I don't think our extension can fix those unless we know if the request is coming from Copilot (references UI not updated) or the user (references UI updated), maybe this can bug can be changed to a feature request for that?

This thread is going off the rails. This is about copilot using local models in VSCode.
Local models have been working in copilot for a long time now!
The issue is/was that there was no way to decouple autocomplete or to make it also use your local models, and you have to sign in to a free copilot account which would get exhausted and then the free plan would get disabled until next month.

So to be clear autocomplete wouldn't use your local models and there wasn't an option to adjust that.

This may be fixed now at least from some news I read where you no longer have to log into copilot, if thats true then it will be good now.

This isn't the right thread to bring up continue or other extensions, those have been working.

You guys are having other kinds of technical issues.

- Send a message to an agent host session in the agents window, ask for edits
- Don't click away from the session
- When it's done, you should see the diffs in the changes view. Previously they were not showing up until reopening the session
